title: The Garden
about: The quiet garden where an already-growing relationship was finally given a name.
description: This track remembers a hidden garden behind the Agriculture Building where the noise of the fair seemed to disappear. Sitting together on a bench, sharing a kiss and an unhurried moment, I finally asked the question I'd been carrying with me: whether she'd go out with me. In many ways we were already together, so her simple yes didn't begin the story as much as give a name to what had already grown between us.
lyrics: Verse 1
We'd started finding corners no one else would see,
Trading crowded walkways for a little privacy.
The fair kept rolling on outside those gates,
While we stole quiet moments from the hands of fate.
Behind the Agriculture Building, tucked away,
There was a little garden at the end of the day.
Just a bench beneath the summer sky,
A place where the world could pass us by.
Pre-Chorus
We didn't need a grand parade...
Just somewhere the noise could fade.
Chorus
In the garden behind the building,
Time forgot to move at all.
You climbed into my lap so naturally,
Like you'd never thought to fall.
A kiss beneath the evening sky,
Your head resting while the world rolled by.
One quiet question... one simple "yes"...
And the garden became our forever.
Verse 2
I remember brushing gently through your hair,
Neither one of us in any kind of hurry there.
The fair was only footsteps far away,
Yet somehow it felt like another place.
I'd been carrying those words for days,
Wondering a hundred different ways.
Then I finally let them leave my heart,
Though we'd already made our start.
Pre-Chorus
Looking back, it's funny now...
We already knew somehow.
Chorus
In the garden behind the building,
Time forgot to move at all.
You climbed into my lap so naturally,
Like the moment knew our names.
I asked if you'd go out with me,
You smiled before you answered me.
One quiet promise... one simple "yes"...
And nothing felt impossible.
Bridge
No cheering crowd...
No spotlight overhead...
No perfect speech I'd planned for weeks,
Just honest words instead.
Maybe we were already together,
Maybe the answer had been there all along.
The question didn't start the story...
It only gave it a name.
Final Chorus
In the garden behind the building,
The summer air stood still.
One little bench, one stolen moment,
One memory that always will.
It isn't fireworks,
It's your smile before you answered,
Your head across my knees.
One quiet garden...
One unforgettable "yes."
